rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not ask about an applicant's criminal record until after a conditional offer. They may never consider arrests without conviction, expunged, pardoned, vacated, juvenile or sealed records. After an offer they may consider only listed serious convictions or recent convictions within look-back periods, and must do an individualized assessment and give written reasons if they withdraw the offer.
rules.key_value: Look-back after conditional offer: 6 years (first-degree), 4 years (second/third-degree), 1 year (fourth-degree); serious listed offenses with no limit
rules.penalty: Civil penalty up to $1,000 (first violation), $5,000 (one prior violation in 5 years), $10,000 (two or more prior violations in 7 years); possible return of application fee and up to $1,000 paid to applicant
rules.status_basis: Approved June 18, 2021; takes effect the first day of the seventh month next following enactment.

exempt_if.text: a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units

coverage.summary: Applies to rental dwelling units offered for rent by housing providers.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Excludes dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.

rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
